name: Yotta Data Services
snippet: Hiranandani-backed Indian data center operator whose Shakti Cloud runs the country's largest Nvidia GPU fleet. It targets about 85,000 GPUs by FY27 and an India IPO in early 2027.

facts.label: Fleet target
facts.value: About 85,000 GPUs by end of FY27

origin: The Hiranandani Group set up Yotta in 2019 to move from real estate into data centers, with Darshan Hiranandani and Sunil Gupta as promoters. The group launched the business in July 2020 with NM1, a Tier IV data center at its Panvel campus in Navi Mumbai. In December 2023 Yotta announced a collaboration with Nvidia to deploy 16,384 H100 GPUs by June 2024 and 32,768 by the end of 2025. That H100 fleet became Shakti Cloud, which Gupta runs as co-founder, MD and CEO.
today: Yotta runs 8,192 H100 and 1,024 L40S GPUs at NM1, and two global customers have contracted all 8,192 of its delivered B200 GPUs at 4,096 each. In 2025 Yotta supplied more than half of the IndiaAI Mission's GPU capacity, including 4,096 GPUs allocated to Sarvam AI and 1,536 to Soket AI Labs. The company says 85 to 90 percent of its new capacity goes to overseas offtakers on long-term contracts. Nvidia has also agreed a four-year DGX Cloud engagement with Yotta worth more than $1B. In March 2026 Gorilla Technology agreed to supply 640 HGX B200 servers, more than 5,000 GPUs, for Yotta to operate at NM1. In July 2026 Yotta raised about $150M from wealthy individuals and family offices at a $3.9B valuation, and in September 2026 the Serum Institute surfaced as an early backer. Its campuses are NM1 (52 MW IT) in Navi Mumbai, D1 (30 MW IT) in Greater Noida and a 1 MW IT site, G1, in GIFT City.
platform: Shakti Cloud rents Nvidia GPUs as bare metal, virtual machines, Kubernetes and Slurm clusters, serverless GPUs and OpenAI-compatible inference endpoints. Shakti Studio adds fine-tuning and model deployment, and Shakti AI Lab serves universities. Clusters use Nvidia Quantum InfiniBand with parallel file and object storage, and in May 2025 Yotta put Shakti Cloud on Nvidia DGX Cloud Lepton. Published bare metal rates are ₹351 per GPU hour for HGX H100 and ₹473 per GPU hour for HGX B200.
outlook: Yotta plans 30,000 B300 GPUs in a 60 MW D2 building at Greater Noida and 36,000 GB300 or Vera Rubin GPUs in a 75 MW NM2 building at Navi Mumbai. In September 2026 its CEO said it plans 40,000 Vera Rubin GPUs at a new Noida site as part of a $12B expansion. The company says it will file its DRHP and list in India between January and March 2027, after dropping an earlier plan to list in the US first. It seeks up to $1.5B across pre-IPO and IPO rounds to fund roughly $7B of AI capex, which leaves the buildout dependent on capital markets and overseas offtake.

editor_notes: The seed's reported $1B+ Blackwell order matches three separate reported items. In September 2025 Yotta ordered 8,190 B200 GPUs described as a $1.5B investment. Nvidia signed a four-year DGX Cloud engagement worth more than $1B. Yotta also announced 20,736 liquid-cooled Blackwell Ultra GPUs backed by over $2B. I could not verify Yotta's exact IndiaAI GPU count or pricing tier, so the profile says only that it supplied more than half of the mission's capacity (the mission's July 2025 aggregate H100 rate was Rs 92 per GPU hour). I found no confirmation that the DRHP was filed as of 2026-10-13. Reported deal sizes vary, with a Rs 6,000 to 8,000 crore issue inside a total raise of up to $1.5B. The Economic Times, Moneycontrol and Livemint items came from Yotta's media page and their sites blocked direct fetching, so I checked only their headlines. The 2019 founding year comes from a secondary unlisted-share report. Gorilla Technology supplies GPUs for Yotta to operate, so the profile treats it as a partner and leaves it off the customer list. A 2026 Vera Rubin plan (40,000 GPUs, $12B) is listed in the outlook but not in accelerators.

name: Neysa
snippet: Mumbai AI cloud founded in 2023 by Netmagic founder Sharad Sanghi. Blackstone took a majority stake in February 2026 with up to $600M of equity to grow it from 1,200 to over 20,000 GPUs.

facts.label: Blackstone-led raise
facts.value: Up to $600M equity plus $600M planned debt (February 2026)

origin: Sharad Sanghi, who founded the Indian data center company Netmagic in 1998 and later sold it to NTT, started Neysa in 2023 with former Netmagic CTO Anindya Das. Exodus Communications founder BV Jagadeesh chairs the company. Neysa set out to give Indian enterprises and the public sector GPU capacity and AI platform services hosted inside India. It raised a $20M seed round led by Matrix Partners India (now Z47) in April 2024, launched its Velocis cloud in July 2024, and closed a $30M Series A co-led by Nexus Venture Partners, NTTVC and Z47 in October 2024.
today: Blackstone funds and co-investors Teachers' Venture Growth, TVS Capital, 360 ONE Asset and Nexus Venture Partners agreed in February 2026 to invest up to $600M of equity in Neysa, which gives Blackstone a majority stake. Neysa plans to raise another $600M of debt against that equity, for a total of up to $1.2B. At the time of the deal it ran about 1,200 GPUs and planned to scale past 20,000 GPUs in India. Sanghi said he expects revenue to more than triple in the following year. The IndiaAI Mission approved Neysa as a cloud service provider in May 2025 and listed it on the mission portal in August 2025, so public users can rent its GPUs at government-negotiated rates. In 2026 Neysa teamed up with Pipeshift on inference in May and with Mavenir in September, and Mavenir now develops and tests its AI products on Neysa infrastructure.
platform: Velocis combines GPU-as-a-service, a managed AI platform, inference endpoints, MLOps orchestration and monitoring, and the Aegis LLM Shield security product. Customers rent Nvidia L4, L40S, H100 and H200 and AMD MI300X GPUs as bare metal, virtual machines or Kubernetes, either on demand or on commitments of 1 to 36 months. Neysa advertises 3,200 Gbps networking and NVMe-backed storage. Its model catalog includes open models such as Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and GPT-OSS.
outlook: Neysa says it will use the Blackstone capital to deploy more than 20,000 GPUs in India. It plans to expand to Malaysia and Japan and later Europe, with access to data centers run by Blackstone's AirTrunk. Sanghi said in May 2026 that Neysa is considering an IPO within 24 to 36 months. The company has not disclosed how many GPUs it has added since the February 2026 round, and the $600M debt remained subject to documentation when the deal was announced.

editor_notes: The seed's $50M in 2024 is the cumulative total of a $20M seed (April 2024, led by Matrix Partners India, now Z47) and a $30M Series A (October 2024, co-led by Nexus, NTTVC and Z47), not a single round. The Blackstone deal is confirmed, with definitive agreements announced 2026-02-16 for up to $600M of equity with a Blackstone majority stake, plus $600M of planned debt. The $1.4B valuation appears only in secondary profiles, not in Neysa or Blackstone releases. I could not verify an Overwatch product on Neysa's current site, and Aegis LLM Shield is confirmed. Neysa's IndiaAI GPU count and its fleet size after February 2026 are not public. Secondary sources give founding years of 2022 and 2024, and the profile uses Neysa's own 2023. The Netmagic founding year and NTT sale come from secondary profiles. Customer names come from Neysa's homepage logo wall.
